title: Family Link Killed Chrome — So Boytasks Got Its Own App | vitalii.no
description:
Boytasks is a family task app, originally built as a Chrome-wrapped PWA. The moment Google's Family Link suspends Chrome on a kid's phone — which it does by design, as a parental control — the whole app disappears for every kid on the plan at once, even though nothing in Boytasks itself had changed.

A separate native Android project now loads the Boytasks site directly inside its own WebView shell, with no dependency on the Chrome package at all. Signing in no longer needs a browser session either: a new PIN-login endpoint takes a 4-digit code, exchanges it for a magic-link token, and verifies it into a real session, with a matching PIN entry screen in the app.

Before this, a single Family Link policy change could take down homework access for all three kids at once. Now the native app keeps working straight through a Chrome suspension, because it never depended on Chrome in the first place.
